public.prompt: A card has `width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 2px solid; box-sizing: content-box`. Ignoring margins, what is its rendered outer width and why?

options.label: `244px`; the width covers content, then 40px of horizontal padding and 4px of borders are added.
`200px`; the declared width already includes content, padding, and borders under content-box.
`240px`; horizontal padding is added to width, while borders do not affect the outer size.

answerProof.summary: With content-box, width sizes the content box; both sides of padding and border expand the rendered border box to 244 pixels.
decisiveConstraints: Padding and border apply on both horizontal sides.

claims.statement: Under content-box, declared width applies to content and padding plus border are added to obtain the outer size.

optionRationales.explanation: The calculation is 200 + 20 + 20 + 2 + 2, producing a 244px border box.
That result describes border-box sizing, not the content-box value specified in the prompt.
optionRationales.plausibility: Many applications globally switch every element to border-box.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: This card explicitly overrides the sizing model to content-box.

optionRationales.explanation: Content-box adds both border widths as well as padding to the outer border-box width.
optionRationales.plausibility: The two 20px padding values are the largest visible additions.
